bait_intel_full.quote: recreational and giant bluefin feeding on bunker, squid, and sand eels from Coxes Ledge to Cape Cod Bay and beyond

bait_intel_full.source: Capt. Scott Worth via OTW LI/NYC report
bait_intel_full.quote: Small sand eels working on 30-55" bluefin — soft plastics like the Joe Baggs Miracle Minnow
huge schools of squid chasing sand eels on the surface — jigging squid and mackerel between tuna bites

bait_intel_full.location: East Atlantis / Montauk inshore tuna grounds
bait_intel_full.quote: Lots of big offshore sand eels showing. Sand eels, squid, even butterfish are being found in [tuna] stomachs. Whales and porpoises in the area.

bait_intel_full.source: Capt. Stu, Northport Charters via OTW
bait_intel_full.quote: Stripers were slamming butterfish on top

bait_intel_full.source: Jay (Pamela May Charters) + Dave (Ocean State Tackle) via OTW
bait_intel_full.quote: Large push of shad locally, beneficial for live-liners. Stripers feeding on an abundance of shad that moved into the area this week.

bait_intel_full.location: Newport, Upper Bay, Cape Cod Canal
bait_intel_full.source: Eric, The Saltwater Edge via OTW
bait_intel_full.quote: Squid still active around Newport, in the Upper Bay, and in the Cape Cod Canal

bait_intel_full.bait: school bluefin busting butterfish + squid + sand eels
bait_intel_full.location: NY / NJ nearshore-midshore (school bluefin bonanza belt)
bait_intel_full.quote: There's a school bluefin bonanza in New York and New Jersey, the giant fishing is lock and load in New England, and the canyons are still on fire.

bait_intel_full.location: Offshore NY (north of Butterfish Hole area)
bait_intel_full.source: Bill Falco, Chasing Tails Bait & Tackle (Oakdale) via OTW LI/NYC report
bait_intel_full.quote: Twenty- to 30-pound fish are destroying schools of butterfish up north, and the Montauk bass are all over the bunker and sand eels.

bait_intel_full.location: Offshore south of Montauk, going airborne under shark feeds
bait_intel_full.source: Capt. Pete Douma, Windward Outfitters (Montauk) via OTW LI/NYC report
bait_intel_full.quote: There have been some really impressive spinner and thresher shark feeds under the schools of mackerel, going completely airborne.

bait_intel_full.bait: hungry bluefin school (jigged 4 at a time)
bait_intel_full.source: Capt. Adrian Moeller, Rockfish Charters (Center Moriches)
bait_intel_full.quote: The amount of life is a great sign, and we managed to find a feed of hungry bluefin, jigging four at a time up to 55 inches!

bait_intel_full.source: Dustin Stevens, RI Kayak Fishing Adventures via OTW RI report
bait_intel_full.quote: Seen bonito. Fall run around corner—book spots ASAP!

bait_intel_full.bait: sand lance / sand eels (inferred from bubble-net feeding behavior)
bait_intel_full.source: CRESLI/Viking Fleet whale watch — 12+ humpbacks bubble-net feeding is a specific sand lance / sand eel indicator
bait_intel_full.quote: Over a dozen humpback cooperatively bubble net feeding — south of Montauk Point lighthouse. Bubble net = concentrated small-forage-fish schools.

whale_sightings_full.quote: Epic conditions — 5 cetacean species logged, 1100+ ID photos reviewed.
3 cetacean species incl. Tamanend's bottlenose dolphins, mild haze, good visibility.

whale_sightings_full.source: OTW Northeast Offshore Report (Jimmy Fee / Anthony DeiCicchi)
whale_sightings_full.quote: Anglers willing to cover water are still finding success around whales, bait, and clean temperature breaks.
Low 70s, light breeze, sunny skies; multiple cetacean species with sporadic activity.
5 species logged — 15-20 bottlenose plus 200 short-beaked common dolphins in multiple groups. Calm seas, unlimited visibility.
Whale watching described as 'ON FIRE' — dolphins and finback whales.
At least 8 finback whales confirmed alongside bottlenose and common dolphins. Dark shoals of bait visible at the surface.

whale_sightings_full.location: East Atlantis / Montauk inshore tuna grounds
whale_sightings_full.quote: Lots of big offshore sand eels showing. Whales and porpoises in the area — sand eels, squid, even butterfish in tuna stomachs.

whale_sightings_full.count: 12+ humpbacks bubble-net feeding, plus minkes and dolphins
whale_sightings_full.quote: Over a dozen humpback cooperatively bubble net feeding — south of Montauk Point lighthouse. Massive bait ball indicator.

whale_sightings_full.count: 8-12 humpbacks (incl. mother/calf pairs), 8 minkes, 60-80 common dolphins
whale_sightings_full.quote: 8-12 humpbacks including mother/calf pairs, 8 minkes, 60-80 short-beaked common dolphins.
Humpbacks, minke whales, bottlenose dolphins — multiple cetacean species encountered.
